title: US Treasury Market Shows Stress as Debt Hits $40 Trillion, AfD Wins First Post-War German State
subhead: Long-term US yields are rising despite weak data, a sign demand for Treasuries is softening as debt tops $40 trillion, while Germany's far-right AfD wins Saxony-Anhalt and Iran's leadership publicly acknowledges the economic toll of the war.

sections.heading: Treasury Market Stress Signals a Shift in Global Demand for US Debt
sections.body:
Robin Brooks, a senior fellow at the Brookings Institution, wrote this week that US policy is now focused on preventing long-term borrowing costs from shooting higher, calling it an 'all-hands-on-deck situation where long-term yields are concerned.' Economic data pointing to weaker activity have failed to bring long-term yields down, breaking the historical pattern and revealing upward pressure coming from the market itself, according to Fortune's reporting on his analysis.

US debt now stands at $40 trillion, and the concern is not confined to Washington. Yields in the UK, France, Germany and Japan are also surging. Foreign central banks and institutions that once anchored demand for Treasuries have pulled back and increasingly turned to gold, while Norges Bank Investment Management, the world's largest sovereign wealth fund with $2.3 trillion in assets, has proposed reshuffling its debt holdings away from Treasuries. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent is doubling debt buybacks, and Fed Chair Kevin Warsh sought to reassure markets on inflation credibility at Jackson Hole.
sections.whyItMatters: If the world's benchmark safe asset loses buyers at the same time the US runs record deficits, the cost of financing the global system rises for everyone — and it compounds the inflation pressure already coming from the Iran war.

sections.heading: Iran's Leadership Publicly Acknowledges Economic Distress
sections.body:
Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei, who has not been seen in public since the US-Israeli strike on February 28 that killed his father, issued a written statement banning officials from 'committing anything that harms social cohesion' and urging them to avoid 'discouraging statements that weaken national and public motivation,' according to Reuters as reported by Fortune. He called for action on 'the chain of economic and livelihood challenges, such as inflation, unemployment, management of prices and the market for goods and services.'

President Masoud Pezeshkian acknowledged in state media that 'we have many problems,' estimating that Iranian trade has plunged 25 to 35 percent. The rial has crashed to 2.2 million per US dollar, down from about 1 million a year ago, and inflation has soared above 80 percent. Senior Iranian sources told Reuters the US blockade and crackdown on sanctions evasion are growing harder to withstand, with Iran holding only about two months of gasoline supplies. Treasury Secretary Bessent has announced an 'economic D-Day' to shut down sanctions-evasion channels.
sections.whyItMatters: A supreme leader who has stayed out of public view since his father's death publicly conceding economic strain is a notable signal that US economic pressure is biting — even if the regime's grip on power remains intact.

sections.heading: AfD Wins Saxony-Anhalt, a First for Post-War Germany
sections.body:
Exit polls show Germany's far-right AfD winning the eastern state of Saxony-Anhalt, according to Al Jazeera, CNN and Fox News. The result marks the first time the party has taken a German state since the post-war era, though it remains unclear whether it will be able to form a government, as other parties have ruled out coalition with it. The New York Times framed the result as a signal to Europe.

The win follows the party's strong national showing and adds pressure on politics in Berlin, where mainstream parties have so far refused to work with the AfD. The outcome is the latest sign of the far right's advance in Germany and across Europe.
sections.whyItMatters: A far-right party winning a state government for the first time in post-war Germany reshapes the country's political arithmetic and sends a signal to the rest of Europe about the durability of the far-right surge.

sections.heading: US Envoys Visit Kyiv as OPEC Holds Oil Output Steady
sections.body:
US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner made a first visit to Ukraine for peace talks, according to Axios, extending a diplomatic track running in parallel to the fighting. The visit follows recent signals from Moscow that a diplomatic path could be open, though no breakthrough has been reported.

Separately, OPEC and its allies agreed to keep oil output steady for October, according to the Wall Street Journal. The decision comes as oil prices have climbed back up on the intensifying US-Iran war and the Hormuz disruption, and as the Treasury market stress described above adds to the inflation picture.
sections.whyItMatters: A steady OPEC decision keeps supply tight just as war-related disruption and a weakening appetite for US debt push energy and financing costs higher, while the Witkoff-Kushner trip keeps a US diplomatic channel to Kyiv open.

sections.heading: Anak Krakatau Eruption Closes Eight Indonesian Airports
sections.body:
The Anak Krakatau volcano erupted, forcing the closure of eight Indonesian airports, according to the BBC. The eruption disrupted air travel across the archipelago, a key node in regional and global shipping and aviation routes.

The event is a reminder of the natural-disaster risk that periodically disrupts Southeast Asia's transport and trade corridors, though no major strategic shift has been reported from the eruption itself.
sections.whyItMatters: Disruption to Indonesian air hubs, even if temporary, ripples through regional logistics at a time when global supply chains are already strained by war and sanctions.

bottomLine: The day's most consequential development is financial rather than military: the US Treasury market is showing signs that demand for the world's benchmark safe asset is softening just as debt hits $40 trillion, a shift that would raise financing costs globally and compound war-driven inflation. In parallel, Iran's supreme leader publicly acknowledged the economic strain of the US campaign, Germany's far right won its first post-war state, and US envoys visited Kyiv while OPEC held output steady. The Iran war and Ukraine diplomacy continue, but the emerging story is the pressure building on the financial architecture that underpins the entire system.
